Chapter III - Page 97
Sir George Godber (British Ministry of Health) under title of the
British and Norweigen Experiences: This is "an exercise which is
quite different from almost anything else that we who are concerned with
preventive medicine have tried or now try to do."
'We know that chronic bronchitis with its large toll of mortality and
even larger morbidity is substantially attributable to smoking."
P.103 'We may be dealing with a situation in which a climate of opinion
will be gradually formed by the steady pressure of information about
the hazards until the smoking of cigarettes becomes no longer an
acceptable activity in public." P.105 "There is much we do not know
about the pharmacology of nicotine and its effect on the maintainance
of the

proportion of the public that believes that there are differences of
opinion among the experts."
Perhaps the disability and deaths from chronic bronchitis which are
so largely the result of cigarette smoking and are in sum no less than
the risk of lung cancer, as well as the greater risk of early heart
disease are too little emphasized.
